description: I am an Information Security professional with 25 years of experience in cybersecurity, penetration testing, AI security, and technology innovation. I am leading FIREGUARD-X ASI, an intelligent prototype focused on interpreting NASA microgravity combustion research for space fire safety. I welcome passionate participants with skills in AI/ML, Python, data science, aerospace engineering, scientific research, UI/UX, and space technology who want to build innovative solutions together.
summary:
FIREGUARD-X ASI is an AI-assisted research prototype developed to explore fire safety challenges in microgravity. It brings together a visual Fire Digital Twin, NASA Evidence Explorer, AI Cognitive Council, AI Debate, Risk Analytics, Trust Center, Security Center and Audit Center in a unified mission command dashboard.

The prototype aims to help users explore microgravity combustion research, examine potential fire scenarios, organise scientific evidence and assess possible safety risks through multiple AI perspectives. Its specialist AI roles represent combustion science, data analysis, risk intelligence, mission safety, adversarial review and scientific oversight.

By combining scientific exploration, risk visualisation, transparency and cybersecurity considerations, FIREGUARD-X ASI addresses the challenge of turning microgravity combustion insights into more accessible and structured fire safety intelligence.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity, making space fire safety an important concern for crew protection and mission continuity. This prototype demonstrates an approach to supporting research and informed safety analysis for future space missions.
details:
FIREGUARD-X ASI — Adaptive Scientific Intelligence for Space Fire Safety

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

FIREGUARD-X ASI is an AI-inspired, multi-agent research prototype designed to explore fire safety challenges in microgravity. It provides a unified Mission Command Center through which users can investigate combustion scenarios, examine potential fire risks and review scientific evidence.

The platform contains nine integrated modules:

  • Mission Command: Presents the mission scenario, risk status and recommended response workflow.
  • Fire Digital Twin: Provides an interactive visual simulation of flame behaviour using adjustable parameters such as oxygen concentration, airflow, temperature, pressure, fuel material, geometry and gravity conditions.
  • AI Cognitive Council: Represents seven specialist roles: Combustion Scientist, NASA Data Scientist, Fire Risk, Mission Safety, Adversarial Red Team, Scientific Guardian and Mission Commander.
  • NASA Evidence Explorer: Organises research-related evidence and displays connections between combustion topics and experimental datasets.
  • AI Debate: Demonstrates how different specialist perspectives can challenge and review a proposed assessment.
  • Trust Center: Calculates a prototype trust score using evidence quality, source relevance, experimental match, agent agreement, adversarial verification, data integrity and uncertainty.
  • Security Center: Demonstrates cybersecurity safeguards, including prompt-injection detection, dataset integrity checks, agent permissions and access-control policies.
  • Risk Analytics: Presents scenario-based risk information and visual comparisons.
  • Audit Center: Records simulated mission events and actions for review.

Users can modify environmental parameters, select predefined scenarios and observe how the prototype's risk and trust calculations respond. The Mission Commander presents recommendations, while human approval remains necessary before simulated mission actions.

2. What benefits does it provide?

FIREGUARD-X ASI brings several aspects of space fire safety research together in one interactive environment.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Making complex microgravity combustion concepts easier to explore.
  • Helping users compare different environmental and material conditions.
  • Organising research evidence alongside scenario-based risk assessments.
  • Encouraging critical review through multiple specialist perspectives.
  • Highlighting uncertainty and insufficient evidence rather than presenting every result as reliable.
  • Demonstrating cybersecurity considerations for AI-assisted scientific systems.
  • Providing an accessible visual environment for students, researchers and space safety enthusiasts.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact is to demonstrate how scientific research, intelligent analysis, transparent decision-support concepts and cybersecurity principles could work together to support future space fire safety research.

Fire behaviour in microgravity can differ from behaviour on Earth. Better ways to explore combustion conditions, evidence limitations and potential risks may help researchers and mission planners investigate important safety questions.

FIREGUARD-X ASI is intended as a research and demonstration prototype, not an operational spacecraft fire-control system or a NASA-validated prediction engine.

4. What tools, coding languages and software were used?

The project started as a browser-based interactive dashboard prototype. It is now a complete Docker-based web application built with:

Frontend (what the user sees)

  • TypeScript and React: The nine dashboard screens, the vertical sidebar and the mission pipeline, with typed, reusable components.
  • Vite: Build tool and development server.
  • Tailwind CSS and CSS3: Responsive layout, styling and visual panels.
  • Recharts and SVG: Risk graphs, heat map, trust gauges and analytics indicators.
  • HTML Canvas: Interactive flame and combustion visualisation.
  • Web Speech API: Indian-English voice narration, spoken alerts and voice commands.
  • Browser Local Storage: Saves the selected voice preferences.
  • nginx: Serves the dashboard and forwards API requests, with security headers.

Backend (the intelligence)

  • Python 3.12 with FastAPI and Pydantic: REST API, strict input validation, risk calculations, the seven-agent council and the AI trust engine.
  • SQLAlchemy and Alembic: Database models and migrations.
  • PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector: Stores NASA documents and evidence vectors for similarity search (retrieval-augmented generation).
  • Redis: Rate limiting and the download job queue.
  • httpx, pypdf and BeautifulSoup: Download and read NASA reports and web pages.
  • SHA-256: Document fingerprints, a sealed manifest, tamper detection and a hash-chained audit log.
  • JWT login, PBKDF2 password hashing and role-based access control: Secure sign-in with viewer, analyst, commander and admin roles.
  • Optional OpenAI API (off by default): Optional embeddings and sentence rewording. It cannot change any score.

Data

  • NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) and science.nasa.gov: Real documents on BASS-II, SoFIE, ACME, Saffire and spacecraft fire safety.
  • NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) CSV files (optional): Real numeric observations.
  • SYNTHETIC/DEMO passages: Offline demo evidence, clearly labelled and never presented as NASA data.

Deployment and quality

  • Docker and Docker Compose: One command starts the frontend, backend, database, Redis and worker.
  • pytest, Vitest, Ruff, mypy and ESLint: 108 backend tests, frontend tests, linting and type checking.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creative aspect of FIREGUARD-X ASI is its combination of a Fire Digital Twin, seven specialist reasoning roles, adversarial review, evidence-oriented analysis and cybersecurity controls within one mission-control interface.

Instead of presenting only a fire-risk score, the prototype demonstrates a workflow in which different specialist roles examine a scenario, challenge assumptions, review evidence and uncertainties, and pass the outcome through a Scientific Guardian and Mission Commander.

It also introduces a security-focused perspective through demonstrations of prompt-injection detection, SHA-256 integrity verification, least-privilege agent permissions and simulated attack scenarios.

This combination of scientific exploration, multi-perspective analysis and security-by-design makes the project distinctive.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The project considered several important factors:

  • Microgravity conditions: How gravity, airflow and oxygen conditions influence combustion scenarios.
  • Fuel and material properties: Different materials, sample geometries and heating conditions.
  • Scientific evidence: The relevance, completeness and limitations of available research information.
  • Uncertainty: Avoiding unsupported conclusions when evidence is insufficient or conditions are outside the represented experimental range.
  • Crew safety: Prioritising human safety and requiring human approval for simulated mission actions.
  • AI reliability: Considering conflicting outputs, unsupported citations and adversarial inputs.
  • Cybersecurity: Protecting evidence integrity and restricting agent permissions.
  • Transparency: Recording simulated events and distinguishing demonstration data from verified scientific results.
  • Usability: Presenting complex information through a unified and understandable mission-control dashboard.

7. Future development

Future work will focus on integrating verified NASA research datasets and source-level citations, connecting independently operating AI agents, validating combustion and risk models against published experimental results, and developing a more comprehensive scientific evaluation framework.

FIREGUARD-X ASI aims to demonstrate a responsible approach to intelligent space fire safety research through the combination of scientific exploration, transparent decision support and cybersecurity.
